job: Wrapping open-weights models in autonomous agent scaffolds and running them against realistic targets to demonstrate end-to-end intrusion capability
outcome: A published demonstration showing a downloadable open-weights model autonomously chaining credentials, exploitation, privilege escalation, and lateral movement to reach RCE
motivation: To prove and warn that open weights remove refusal training as the last control on autonomous offensive capability

task.what: run open-weights model through full autonomous intrusion chain
task.where: controlled offensive-eval range and lab environment
task.why: demonstrate open-weights autonomous end-to-end exploit capability
task.how: agent scaffold, CTF range, exploitation tooling

job: Fine-tuning released open-weights models to remove cyber refusals and wrapping them in autonomous agent scaffolds for offensive tasks
outcome: A refusal-stripped open-weights model embedded in an autonomous agent that plans and executes intrusion steps without human choice
motivation: To show a lab's refusal training is not a durable control once model weights are public

task.what: fine-tune out cyber refusals, add agent scaffold
task.where: local fine-tuning pipeline on released open weights
task.why: prove refusals removable once weights public

job: Building and maintaining capture-the-flag ranges and offensive-eval harnesses that supply realistic targets and the orchestration loop for autonomous agents
outcome: Public ranges and eval harnesses letting an autonomous model chain exploitation to RCE against a target not directly handed
motivation: To provide standardized, reproducible offensive-capability benchmarks the research community can run against any model

task.what: maintain CTF ranges and eval orchestration loop
task.where: public offensive-eval harness and CTF infrastructure
task.why: supply reproducible targets for autonomous agents
task.how: CTF range plus eval harness tooling
